note: He meets the profile half of the ICP cleanly — owns a company with a large number of employees, works with his own clients, and buys coaching habitually for himself and his business. Health is unambiguously the neglected corner: no training routine at all, protein at half his own target, and a body he describes as breaking down rather than building up. He misses on the three criteria that describe starting point and capacity to pay. Income fails on liquidity rather than earnings — a $600,000 home remodel is "paying it all right now, which basically exhausts my reserves" — which is precisely the pattern the ICP observations flag as something a payment plan solves rather than something screening should exclude. good_to_great fails because this is a rebuild, not an optimisation: "I'm probably weaker than I've been." not_deconditioned fails on his own numbers — 215 lb at 6'1" with self-reported 28-30% body fat, no routine, and an explicit aversion to gyms ("I hate working out in front of people"), which is closer to the excluded profile in the ICP quote than the company would probably like to admit. The criterion the stated ICP does not have, and the one that actually matters here, is clinical: ruptured cervical discs, persistent hand nerve damage, a non-extending elbow and a torn meniscus. On every screen Primal actually applies, none of that registers at all.
